name: Prince Skyline GT (S54A)
hook: To beat the rules, Prince stretched a family saloon by 200 millimetres, crammed in a six, and built a hundred road cars just in time to race.
story:
Spring 1964. Japan's second Grand Prix is coming to Suzuka, and Prince Motor wants the GT class.

Its Skyline is a modest family saloon with a four-cylinder engine. Not enough.

So the team, led by Shinichiro Sakurai, gets radical. They stretch the wheelbase by 200 millimetres. Now the six-cylinder engine from the bigger Gloria fits under a long new nose.

But the rules want road cars. One hundred of them. The team builds them in a rush and only just makes it.

The race cars get the good parts. Three Italian Weber carburettors. A close-ratio five-speed box. A limited-slip differential.

Then a private Porsche 904 turns up. A real mid-engined racer. It should walk away.

It doesn't, not at first. The Skyline hangs on in the corners. Tetsu Ikuzawa dives past the Porsche just before a hairpin, and the crowd goes wild. For a moment, a stretched saloon leads.

The Porsche wins in the end. Skylines take second to sixth. A legend starts right here.
description: The Skyline GT (S54A-1) was a special that Prince Motor built to win the GT-II race at the 2nd Japan Grand Prix in May 1964. Engineers lengthened the Skyline 1500 (S50) wheelbase by 200 mm to fit the Gloria's G7 inline six, and built the 100 road cars the homologation rules required. Road cars had a single carburettor and 105 PS. Race cars ran triple Webers. A Porsche 904 won, but Skylines filled second to sixth, starting the Skyline's racing story.
